meta.title: 3D bioprinting of human neural tissues with functional connectivity.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: A soft fibrin-based bioink and a commercial bioprinter were used to print layered human neural tissues from stem cell-derived progenitors. Printed neurons formed functional circuits between layers within weeks, and astrocyte progenitors matured into astrocytes.

formulations.review_notes: Viability given as 'about 80%'. Also compared: Matrigel (92% viable, clogged the nozzle) and hyaluronic acid (85%).
formulations.name: Soft fibrin gel (2.5 mg/mL fibrinogen, 0.5 U thrombin)
formulations.composition_detail: 2.5 mg/mL fibrinogen gelled with 0.5 U thrombin (gelation ~145 s)
formulations.cell_type: cortical neural progenitors and astrocyte progenitors
formulations.key_outcome: Printed neurons formed functional cortical-to-striatal circuits; about 80% of cells stayed viable for 7 days.

evidence.quote: We chose 2.5 mg/mL fibrinogen and 0.5 U thrombin for hydrogel construction, yielding a gelation time of about 145 ± 10 seconds
more than 85% of the cells survived after 6 hours of culturing in the fibrin gel and about 80% of the cells retained viable for 7 days
The cortical NPCs, differentiated from GFP- or mCherry-labeled hESCs for 21 days, expressed forebrain cortical progenitor markers FOXG1 and PAX6
The cells were centrifuged and resuspended with 20 mg/mL fibrinogen solution at a density of 1 × 107/mL.
